tasks.extracted: In the photographs of strips dipped in fentanyl at 125, 100, 83, 63, 50, 25 and 5 ng/mL, those at 125 to 63 ng/mL show no test band, those at 50 and 25 ng/mL a faint but visible test band, and the strip at 5 ng/mL a strong band; the Methods state that a pink band in the test area means fentanyl is not present. The 25 ng/mL limit by eye therefore counts a faint visible band as positive; under the stated rule the lowest pictured concentration read positive would be 63 ng/mL. The image-analysis threshold (1152 counts at 25 ng/mL) is the intensity of that faint band. tasks.source_read: publisher full text (HTML), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12954-023-00921-8 (saved text with figure notes)
tasks.extracted: The 2017 lots were tested over narrow ranges only, with lower concentrations not tested: diphenhydramine at 150 and 100 mg/mL (positive) and 50 mg/mL (negative); lidocaine at 150 and 100 (positive) and 50 and 25 mg/mL (negative); MDMA at 50 (positive) and 25 mg/mL (negative); methamphetamine at 10 and 5 (positive) and 2.5 mg/mL (negative). The 2021 lots read positive with lidocaine down to 2.5 mg/mL, with MDMA down to 5 (lots 018 and 188) or 2.5 mg/mL (lot 196), with methamphetamine down to 10 mg/mL (negative at 5), and with diphenhydramine from 25 down to 0.5–1 mg/mL, but negative or invalid with diphenhydramine at 50 mg/mL and negative on two lots at 100 mg/mL. So the lidocaine, MDMA and methamphetamine changes are shown by both sets of lots at the same concentrations, while the 2017 lots' diphenhydramine threshold is unknown. tasks.locator: Table 3, note g (PubMed Central copy, PMC12076174); publisher HTML: Methods › Covariates, 1st paragraph; Statistical Analysis, 1st paragraph; Table 3, nonfatal overdose row
tasks.source_read: PMC full text PMC12076174 (Table 3 notes, read by AI reader 147); publisher full text (HTML), https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2833888, saved page text (scratchpad/vickers_page.txt)
tasks.extracted: Covariates were prespecified for the model of each outcome (publisher page, Methods), and the adjusted nonfatal overdose estimate carries its own table note (g), unlike the behaviour estimates (d). As read in the PubMed Central copy, note g lists for the overdose model: baseline strip use, state, age, race, ethnicity and sex, and, for each drug-use day, the drug category, study week, part of the week, the composite risk-reduction score and the number of times strips were used. Injecting, past 30-day overdose, ever having received strip instructions, education and employment are not in it (past overdose and strip instructions are in the behaviour models, note d; injecting is in neither). Editors' reading: the follow-up score and strip-use count come after the exposure and may carry part of any effect, which could pull the adjusted ratio towards 1.
